data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 proposes a lineage-dependency tax (translation cost, ownership loss) as the suppression mechanism but never grounds that mechanism in anything observable within a single run. The problem explicitly asks to 'identify what evidence within a single run would distinguish suppression from mere efficiency' and to 'say exactly what to count' for any countable claim. SRC_001 supplies four counterconditions but no run-internal discriminator and no counting prescription: there is no specified quantity (e.g., number of cross-lineage borrow attempts vs. same-lineage successors, translation-cost delta, ownership-transfer rate) whose measured value would separate the posited suppression tax from an efficient decomposition. Under a causal-mechanism demand this is a structural omission: the mechanism is asserted qualitatively, but the problem's evidential/counting standard is unmet.
